ground_truth: The ball constantly falls on the spring board and triggers it. As soon the blimp reaches it the spring board triggers a diagonal fly
response:
Because the arch is curved the blimp wasn’t sitting on a flat horizontal surface. The arch’s curved contact gives a sideways (horizontal) component to the reaction force when the blimp lifts, and the blimp’s buoyant lift gives the vertical component — result: a diagonal net velocity. In addition, if the blimp was slightly overlapping the arch when the run started the collision-resolution will “pop” it off at an angle, adding horizontal speed.

How to make it go straight up
- Put the blimp exactly centered on a flat top (flat wall or platform) instead of the arch.
- Add short walls/barriers on either side of the blimp to block any horizontal motion.
- Move it slightly so it isn’t overlapping the arch at start.

Any of those will remove the horizontal push and make the blimp rise straight.
